messages:
marta_cust: Hey team — we're seeing streaming responses from the Redwood API cut out around ~60s for long-running responses. Client sees partial SSE events and then connection closed. Reconnects sometimes get 500s. This started after migrating behind an ALB + Cloudflare. Help?

amaya: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a minimal repro (curl) and any headers the client is sending + any error text from the client? Also which deployment (hosted/dedicated/private)?

marta_cust: Hosted (account org-zz). Minimal repro: I curl the chat-stream endpoint and leave it idle while model thinks. After about a minute the connection is closed. Example:  
```bash
curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \\n  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate/stream?model=llama-xyz"
```
Client sees: 
- a few SSE events, then \"recv returned 0\" / connection reset by peer
- when client reconnects quickly we get a 500 from the API for one attempt, then normal.
Headers we see (from client): 
- Accept: text/event-stream
- Connection: keep-alive
- User-Agent: python-requests/2.31

simon: Thanks — that pattern smells like a proxy/load-balancer idle timeout or buffer flush issue. ALB default idle timeout is 60s. If the server doesn't send bytes for >idle timeout, ALB closes connection. If there's buffering in front (nginx/Envoy) the actual data may not be flushed to the socket, so the ALB sees silence.

Quick checklist: 
1) Do you have an ALB in front of the origin? (sounds like yes)
2) Is Cloudflare in front as well? CF can buffer for certain responses unless chunked streaming is detected.
3) Are you using any reverse proxies (nginx/Envoy) between app and ALB?

li: I can check our infra. ALB idle timeout is currently 60s for that target group. There's also an internal nginx reverse proxy on the app nodes.

amaya: Two quick mitigations while we root-cause: 
- increase ALB idle timeout to 300s (if possible)
- ensure server sends periodic keepalive/heartbeat bytes at <60s intervals (15s is safe) — for SSE a comment line like `:\n\n` works.

simon: Also check nginx proxy_buffering and flush behavior. For SSE you want to disable buffering and force flush to the client after every event. Example nginx snippet to add to the location serving streaming: 
```nginx
proxy_buffering off;
proxy_cache off;
proxy_http_version 1.1;
proxy_set_header Connection "";
proxy_set_header X-Accel-Buffering no; # for some app servers
chunked_transfer_encoding on;
```
and on upstream app ensure you call flush after writing each SSE event (fflush / resp.flush). If you're using Go net/http set `w.(http.Flusher).Flush()` after each write.

marta_cust: We use a small node proxy that forwards to the runtime. Not sure it's flushing. Is there anything Cloudflare-specific? We need to support customers behind CF.

simon: Cloudflare will buffer responses for certain cases and may not behave like a pure TCP passthrough. To maximize chance CF will stream: 
- Use HTTP/1.1 with Transfer-Encoding: chunked and send chunks frequently. 
- Set header `Cache-Control: no-transform` and `X-Accel-Buffering: no` (some proxies respect it). 
- If using Cloudflare Workers or the CDN, there are settings around "Origin Response Buffering"; older CF setups may still buffer small responses. Some customers put Cloudflare in front and see ~60s drops because CF will hold until the origin completes a chunk.

rachael: Also flagging product — we should document recommended headers and heartbeating for hosted API customers behind ALBs/CF. Could be a common customer FAQ.

marta_cust: Ok trying quick fixes now — bump ALB timeout and add periodic comments from our app. Patch below (node pseudocode): 
```js
res.setHeader('Content-Type','text/event-stream');
res.setHeader('Cache-Control','no-cache, no-transform');
res.setHeader('Connection','keep-alive');
res.write(': heartbeat\n\n'); // send every 15s via setInterval
res.flush();
```

(we don't have resume-by-id; we just reconnect and expect the app to continue from new request)

amaya: That should help prevent the ALB from idling out. If you still see connection closed with `upstream prematurely closed connection` errors, capture the exact message from our edge logs (we can look from our side).

simon: Additional Envoy / ALB notes: 
- Envoy: set `upstream_http2_protocol_options: {}` if using http2 — but main thing: `common_http_protocol_options.idle_timeout` and `upstream_flush_config` (e.g., flush_interval: 1s) — this forces Envoy to flush buffered data to downstream. 
- For ALB in AWS, edit Target Group > Attributes > Idle timeout (default 60s).

li: Quick infra check: internal nginx had `proxy_buffering on` for that location. I'm going to toggle `proxy_buffering off` and increase ALB idle to 300s in staging to validate.

marta_cust: After adding heartbeat and bumping ALB to 300s I still saw one disconnect but much less frequent. Logs from our client show: 
```
socket.error: [Errno 104] Connection reset by peer
```
Also our node proxy logs show: 
```
[nginx] 2026-02-01T14:12:05 upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream
```

simon: That nginx log confirms the upstream (the runtime) closed the socket. Does the runtime log show anything? Could be the runtime hit an internal timeout or OOM and reset. If you can share the runtime request id (X-Request-Id) from the failed attempt we can correlate.

marta_cust: One request id from 1761234571 attempt: req-8a7c. We see in the runtime logs: 
```
WARN runtime/stream: client reconnect detected, last-event-id=
ERROR runtime/serve: write tcp 10.1.2.5:39212->10.1.2.8:34567: write: broken pipe
```

simon: OK that suggests the runtime was still trying to write but the kernel reported broken pipe — likely because an intermediate proxy had closed the connection. Two likely culprits now: (a) some proxy between runtime and nginx closed the connection due to its own idle setting, (b) the runtime attempted to write a very large chunk (rare) and upstream closed mid-write.

Suggested next steps: 
- li: grep proxy configs for other idle/read_timeout values (any haproxy/NLB timeouts). Check tcp_keepalive settings on the nodes.
- marta_cust: keep sending heartbeats from app + client reconnection logic with exponential backoff. Include `Last-Event-ID`/event-id headers if you have event ids.
- simon: we'll add a small server-side guard so that the runtime will emit a periodic keepalive comment by default for hosted customers behind known ALB/CF frontends (opt-in for now). 

li: I found an internal haproxy instance with timeout client 60s; that was between nginx and ALB for legacy traffic. I bumped it to 400s in staging. Will push to prod after smoke tests.

amaya: Great. Marta — can you confirm after both changes (heartbeat + timeouts) whether the disconnects stop in prod? If they persist include a capture of `tcpdump -w` during a failing session and we'll inspect packets.

marta_cust: Will do. One last question: is there an upstream config on Redwood side we should know about? Eg. do you set `Connection: close` somewhere?

simon: We avoid `Connection: close` for streaming routes. In hosted we route through an ingress (Envoy) configured with a 5m idle_timeout for streaming paths in most regions, but the customer-facing ALB/CF in front can still be the limiting piece. Also we will try to default to emitting a 10s heartbeat for streaming endpoints as a platform-level mitigation.

deploy-bot: rolling deploy started: ingress: add streaming-heartbeat feature flag (canary 10%)

rachael: I'll capture this thread into a short KB (support article) describing: 
- symptoms (disconnect ~60s)
- root cause patterns (ALB idle, proxy_buffering, Cloudflare buffering)
- mitigations (heartbeat, set ALB idle, disable proxy_buffering, nginx/Envoy snippets, headers)
- repro curl snippet + logs to collect

marta_cust: Thanks everyone — will follow up after we validate in prod tomorrow. Appreciate the quick triage.
